source.publisher: Ministerio de Cultura del Perú, Base de Datos de Pueblos Indígenas u Originarios

facts.text: In Peru's 2017 national census, 55,493 people identified as part of the Asháninka people.

source.title: Ashaninka | BDPI
source.publisher: Ministerio de Cultura del Perú, Base de Datos de Pueblos Indígenas u Originarios

nations.name: Confederated Tribes of Siletz Indians
nations.lands: Siletz, on the central Oregon coast; ancestral territory across western Oregon into southwest Washington and northern California

facts.text: After lobbying Congress, the Confederated Tribes of Siletz Indians won repeal of federal termination in 1977.
The Tribe's Athabaskan language dictionary, Nuu-wee-ya' (Our words), holds about 12,000 entries, and a Talking Dictionary lets learners hear words spoken aloud.

source.title: Language - Confederated Tribes of Siletz Indians

nations.name: Timbisha Shoshone Tribe
nations.lands: Death Valley and surrounding areas of California and Nevada

facts.text: Today the federally recognized Timbisha Shoshone Tribe works to keep its language, traditions and sovereignty strong.

source.title: Timbisha Shoshone Tribe - California and Nevada

facts.text: The Timbisha, part of the larger Western Shoshone people, have lived in Death Valley and its surrounding areas for thousands of years, and their village sits inside Death Valley National Park.

source.title: Timbisha Shoshone Tribe - California and Nevada

nations.name: Cahuilla Band of Indians
nations.lands: Anza area, Riverside County, Southern California

facts.text: The Band describes itself as a sovereign nation that carries its culture forward through strong governance.
Cahuilla traditional territory spans a large area of what are now Riverside and San Diego counties.

pronounce.text: kuh-WEE-eh (written on the Band's site as kəˊwi:e)
pronounce.publisher: Cahuilla Band of Indians, on its own site

nations.name: Washoe Tribe of Nevada and California
nations.lands: Lake Tahoe region and nearby valleys of western Nevada and eastern California

facts.text: Washoe teachers hold language classes for adults and youth four days a week, and immersion classes reach children in the tribe's Head Start.

source.title: Where Wašiw is Spoken: The Washoe Tribe is Passing Its Unique Language On and Up
source.publisher: Smithsonian National Museum of the American Indian (American Indian magazine)

facts.text: The name Tahoe is thought to come from Da ow ga, the Washoe word for lake.

source.title: Discover History
source.publisher: USDA Forest Service, Lake Tahoe Basin Management Unit

nations.name: Confederated Tribes and Bands of the Yakama Nation
nations.lands: South-central Washington State, around Mount Adams and tributaries of the Columbia River

facts.text: The Yakama Nation shares an Ichishkiin word each day to help learners build fluency in the language, also called Sahaptin.

source.title: Ichishkiin Word of the Day: Learn New Vocabulary | Yakama Nation
source.publisher: Confederated Tribes and Bands of the Yakama Nation

facts.text: The Yakama Reservation in Washington State spans about 1,130,000 acres.

source.title: About
source.publisher: Confederated Tribes and Bands of the Yakama Nation

nations.name: Santa Ynez Band of Chumash Indians
nations.lands: Santa Ynez Valley, Santa Barbara County, California

facts.text: The Tribe's Culture Department founded its language program in 2008, and the Tribe has unveiled a Samala-English Dictionary.

source.title: Culture
source.publisher: Santa Ynez Band of Chumash Indians

facts.text: Established on December 27, 1901, the Santa Ynez Reservation began with 99 acres and has grown to more than 1,500 acres.

source.title: The Santa Ynez Reservation
source.publisher: Santa Ynez Band of Chumash Indians

nations.name: Tongva
nations.lands: Greater Los Angeles region of California, a homeland called Tovaangar

facts.text: The conservancy, a Tongva-led nonprofit and not a tribal government, serves Tongva people, the wider Native community and guests, called kuuyam.
In 2022 Huhuunga, a one-acre parcel in Altadena, was returned to Tongva stewardship. It is now home to the Tongva-led Tongva Taraxat Paxaavxa Conservancy.

nations.name: Muckleshoot Indian Tribe
nations.lands: South King County, Washington, in the Puget Sound region; ancestors include Duwamish and Upper Puyallup peoples

facts.text: The Muckleshoot Indian Tribe is one of South King County's largest employers, supporting about 3,300 direct jobs.
Among Puget Sound tribes, Muckleshoot is the only one holding rights under two treaties.

nations.name: Tulalip Tribes
nations.lands: Tulalip Indian Reservation on Puget Sound, Snohomish County, Washington

facts.text: The Tulalip Lushootseed Language Department works toward every tribal home, workplace, gathering and classroom being rich in Lushootseed.
The Tulalip Tribes count over 5,100 people, about 2,700 of whom live on the 22,000-acre Tulalip Indian Reservation.

pronounce.publisher: Tulalip Tribes, on its own site

nations.name: Kashia Band of Pomo Indians
also: Kashia Band of Pomo Indians of the Stewarts Point Rancheria
nations.lands: Sonoma County coast of California, from the Gualala River south toward the Russian River

facts.text: The Kashia Band owns the 688-acre Kashia Coastal Reserve, which spans both sides of Highway 1 just north of Salt Point State Park.
Kashia homelands reached from the Gualala River in the north to Duncan's Point, south of the Russian River.

nations.name: Confederated Tribes of the Warm Springs
nations.lands: Central Oregon, stretching east from the summit of the Cascade Mountains

facts.text: The Museum at Warm Springs shares the history and culture of the three tribes and welcomes visitors in Ichishkiin, Numu and Kiksht.

source.title: Museum at Warm Springs - Culture. History. In Living Color.

facts.text: In 1937 the Warm Springs, Wasco and Paiute organized as one confederated government under their own constitution and bylaws.

nations.name: Tolowa Dee-ni' Nation
nations.lands: Smith River and the coast of Del Norte County, far northern California

facts.text: The Tolowa Dee-ni' Nation was restored in 1983 through a court case, and its restored government extended citizenship to all Taa-laa-wa Dee-ni'.
Tolowa Dee-ni' language work goes back to a language program formed in 1969, and the Nation calls revitalization vital to Tolowa identity.

nations.name: Makah Tribe
nations.lands: Neah Bay and Cape Flattery, at the northwest tip of Washington's Olympic Peninsula

facts.text: The name Makah came from neighboring tribes and means people generous with food.
The Makah Reservation at Neah Bay sits on the northwest tip of the continental United States.

nations.name: Confederated Tribes of the Umatilla Indian Reservation
nations.lands: Umatilla Indian Reservation in northeastern Oregon, home of the Cayuse, Umatilla and Walla Walla peoples

facts.text: CTUIR teaches the Umatilla, Walla Walla and Weyíiletpuu (Cayuse) languages to all ages, drawing on the knowledge of fluent speakers.

source.title: Languages of the CTUIR
source.publisher: Confederated Tribes of the Umatilla Indian Reservation

facts.text: Nixyáawii, the homeland name used by the Tribes' language program, means the place of many springs.

source.title: Languages of the CTUIR
source.publisher: Confederated Tribes of the Umatilla Indian Reservation

nations.name: Te-Moak Tribe of Western Shoshone Indians
nations.lands: Northeastern Nevada, in Battle Mountain, Elko, South Fork and Wells

facts.text: The Te-Moak Tribe unites four bands, Battle Mountain, Elko, South Fork and Wells, under one tribal council elected every three years.
Western Shoshone people are descendants of an ancient, widespread people whose name, Newe, means The People.

nations.name: Mam
nations.lands: Western highlands of Guatemala (Huehuetenango, San Marcos, Quetzaltenango) and neighboring Chiapas, Mexico

facts.text: In October 2025, the Mam communities of Cajolá and Todos Santos Cuchumatán joined two other Maya communities in reporting to a UN committee on their community radio rights.

source.title: Indigenous Communities and Cultural Survival Urge CERD to Address Community Radio Rights Violations in Guatemala

facts.text: B'alam Stereo in Cabricán, among the longer-running Indigenous stations in Guatemala's highlands, has served the Maya Mam since 1976, with work promoting education, health, water and justice.

source.title: Announcing Our 2019 Community Media Grants Partners

nations.name: Lokono
nations.lands: Coastal and river villages of Suriname, Guyana and French Guiana

facts.text: Suriname's association of Indigenous village leaders lists the Lokono among the country's four major Indigenous peoples, with villages such as Washabo, Apoera and Alfonsdorp.

source.title: Dorpen en Dorpsbesturen
source.publisher: Vereniging van Inheemse Dorpshoofden in Suriname (VIDS)

facts.text: Lokono village representatives founded Wadian Bokotothi, meaning 'Language Keepers', and helped share one common Lokono spelling across Suriname, French Guiana and Guyana.

source.title: State-of-the-Art in the Development of the Lokono Language
source.publisher: Language Documentation & Conservation, University of Hawai'i Press

nations.name: Ch'orti'
nations.lands: Jocotán, Camotán, Olopa and Quezaltepeque in Chiquimula and La Unión in Zacapa, Guatemala, and communities around Copán in Honduras

facts.text: Ch'orti' is also spoken in Honduran communities such as Cabañas, Santa Rita and Copán Ruinas.

source.title: Descubre los útiles escolares en idioma ch'orti'

facts.text: In 2025 the Academy of Mayan Languages of Guatemala translated the national symbols into Ch'orti'; the flag, for example, is tz'apray b'ujk.

source.title: Símbolos patrios en ch'orti: un aporte para preservar el idioma y la identidad

nations.name: Bribri
nations.lands: The Talamanca mountains of southern Costa Rica, on both the Caribbean (Limón) and Pacific (Puntarenas) sides, with smaller communities in Bocas del Toro, Panama

facts.text: The Bribri language is spoken on both sides of Costa Rica's Talamanca mountains, in Limón and Puntarenas, in three regional varieties named for Amubre, Coroma and Salitre.
Bribri communities also live in Panama, where the 2023 census counted 766 Bribri people.

source.title: Cuadro 20. Población indígena en la República, por sexo, según provincia, comarca indígena, grupo indígena al que pertenece y grupos de edad: Censo 2023
source.publisher: Instituto Nacional de Estadística y Censo (INEC), Panama

nations.name: Tz'utujil
nations.lands: The southern shore of Lake Atitlán in Sololá, Guatemala, including Santiago Atitlán and San Pedro La Laguna

facts.text: In Santiago Atitlán, a Tz'utujil traditional authority welcomed Indigenous youth from three countries in 2013 and spoke in Tz'utujil about the role of ancestral authorities.

source.title: Indigenous Mayan Youth Forge International Relationships Based on Community Radio

facts.text: Radio Sembrador, a community station in San Pedro La Laguna on Lake Atitlán, broadcasts news and cultural programs in Tz'utujil and Spanish.

source.title: Profile of A Community Radio Station: Radio Sembrador

nations.name: Ixil
nations.lands: The Ixil region of northern Quiché, Guatemala: Nebaj, Chajul and Cotzal

facts.text: Ixil women weavers of the Q'imb'al initiative, with youth and village ancestral authorities, launched Community Radio Tiichajil Tenam in Nebaj to share Ixil cultural values.

source.title: Radio Tiichajil Tenam Becomes a Reality

facts.text: In 2020 Guatemala's Constitutional Court ruled in favor of the Maya Ixil people of Nebaj, restoring their ownership of the communal land of Ak'ul.

source.title: Pueblos Mayas Ixiles y Ch'orti's recuperan certeza jurídica sobre sus tierras

nations.name: Kaqchikel
nations.lands: Central highlands of Guatemala, including Chimaltenango, Sacatepéquez and parts of Sololá

facts.text: Community Radio Naköj in Santo Domingo Xenacoj, working since 2013, produces programs in Kaqchikel and Spanish for about 7,000 Kaqchikel listeners.

source.title: 2020 Community Media COVID-19 Emergency Grant Partners

facts.text: In 2022 the United Nations Special Rapporteur on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples was a member of the Maya Kaqchikel people.

source.title: Historic Win: Inter-American Court of Human Rights Rules in Favor of Indigenous Peoples

nations.name: Kaliña
nations.lands: Coastal Suriname and French Guiana, with related communities in Guyana, Venezuela and Brazil

facts.text: In Suriname the Kari'na (Kaliña) live in many villages with their own village heads, including Christiaankondre and Langamankondre at Galibi in Marowijne district.

source.title: Dorpen en Dorpsbesturen
source.publisher: Vereniging van Inheemse Dorpshoofden in Suriname (VIDS)

facts.text: Suriname's Indigenous village leaders say legal recognition of collective rights is an obligation, not a policy choice, and in 2026 urged full implementation of the Kaliña and Lokono judgment.

source.title: VIDS dient resolutie in: Voer Kaliña & Lokono-vonnis uit
source.publisher: Vereniging van Inheemse Dorpshoofden in Suriname (VIDS)

nations.name: Nahuat Pipil
nations.lands: Western El Salvador, especially Sonsonate and Ahuachapán departments

facts.text: Izalco is the only municipality in El Salvador with an ancestral Indigenous government, made up of mayordomos and mayordomas.

source.title: Radio Sensunat: Broadcasting to Revitalize the Nahuat Language in El Salvador

facts.text: In Santo Domingo de Guzmán, Nahuat-speaking teachers created Nahuatl cribs where children learn the language, and Radio Sensunat promotes Nahuat Pipil culture.

source.title: Radio Sensunat: Broadcasting to Revitalize the Nahuat Language in El Salvador

nations.name: Wayuu
nations.lands: The Guajira Peninsula, shared by northern Colombia (La Guajira) and northwestern Venezuela (Zulia)

facts.text: Wayuu justice rests on dialogue: respected mediators called Pütchipü'üi, or palabreros, settle disputes between clans through repair and compensation. UNESCO listed this system in 2010.

source.title: Wayuu normative system, applied by the Pütchipü'üi (palabrero)

facts.text: The Wayuu live on the Guajira Peninsula, which spans the border between Colombia and Venezuela.

source.title: Wayuu normative system, applied by the Pütchipü'üi (palabrero)

nations.name: Ngäbe
nations.lands: The Ngäbe-Buglé comarca in western Panama (parts of Bocas del Toro, Chiriquí and Veraguas), nearby lands in Panama, and Ngäbe territories in southern Costa Rica

facts.text: Panama's Law 10 of 1997 created the Ngäbe-Buglé comarca and made its lands the collective property of the comarca, closed to private sale.

source.title: Ley 10 de 7 de marzo de 1997, por la cual se crea la Comarca Ngöbe-Buglé
source.publisher: FAOLEX, Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations

facts.text: Panama's 2023 census counted 444,878 Ngäbe people.

source.title: Cuadro 20. Población indígena en la República, por sexo, según provincia, comarca indígena, grupo indígena al que pertenece y grupos de edad: Censo 2023
source.publisher: Instituto Nacional de Estadística y Censo (INEC), Panama

nations.name: Guna
nations.lands: Gunayala on Panama's Caribbean coast and islands, plus Madungandí and Wargandí in Panama and communities in northwestern Colombia

facts.text: Gunayala's 49 communities govern themselves together through the Guna General Congress, their highest political and administrative body for land, resources and education.

source.title: Gunayala: A Living Model of Autonomy and Self-government

facts.text: Gunayala runs along Panama's Caribbean coast to the Colombian border, with about 315 km of coastline and over 400 small islands and islets.

source.title: Gunayala: A Living Model of Autonomy and Self-government

nations.name: Emberá
nations.lands: The Emberá-Wounaan comarca and collective lands in Darién and eastern Panama, and the Pacific and Chocó regions of Colombia

facts.text: Panama's Law 22 of 1983 created the Emberá comarca in Darién and named its General Congress the highest traditional decision-making body of the Emberá people.

source.title: Ley 22 de 1983, por la cual se crea la Comarca Emberá de Darién
source.publisher: FAOLEX, Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations

facts.text: Bilingual storybooks in Emberá and Spanish are among the learning materials made for the early education of Emberá children in Panama.

source.title: La educación intercultural bilingüe en Panamá
source.publisher: UNICEF Latin America and the Caribbean

nations.name: Binnizá
nations.lands: The Isthmus of Tehuantepec, Oaxaca, Mexico, including Juchitán and Tehuantepec

facts.text: Velas, festivals honoring patron saints, family names, trades and places, are a central Binnizá institution; Juchitán alone celebrates about 24 of them.

source.title: Zapotecos (del Istmo, Valles centrales y Sierra Norte) : Pueblos indígenas México : Sistema de Información Cultural-Secretaría de Cultura
source.publisher: Secretaría de Cultura, Sistema de Información Cultural (SIC), Gobierno de México

nations.name: Tutunakú
nations.lands: The Totonacapan: northern Veracruz around Papantla and the Sierra Norte de Puebla, Mexico

facts.text: Community groups asked for radio in their own languages, and since 1994 La Voz de la Sierra Norte in Cuetzalan, Puebla has served Nahua and Totonac peoples.

source.title: XECTZ La Voz de la Sierra Norte (AM) : Radio cultural indígena México : Sistema de Información Cultural-Secretaría de Cultura
source.publisher: Secretaría de Cultura, Sistema de Información Cultural (SIC), with station information from INPI

facts.text: At the Centre for Indigenous Arts, Totonac is the language of teaching, and each art is taught in its own house-school, laid out like a traditional settlement.

source.title: Xtaxkgakget Makgkaxtlawana: the Centre for Indigenous Arts and its contribution to safeguarding the intangible cultural heritage of the Totonac people of Veracruz, Mexico

nations.name: Ayuuk
nations.lands: The Sierra Mixe of northeastern Oaxaca, Mexico, including Tlahuitoltepec, Tamazulapam, Ayutla and Guichicovi

facts.text: Backstrap loom weaving continues in Tamazulapam, Tlahuitoltepec and Cotzocón, and young Ayuuk artists are taking up mural and canvas painting.

source.title: Mixes : Pueblos indígenas México : Sistema de Información Cultural-Secretaría de Cultura
source.publisher: Secretaría de Cultura, Sistema de Información Cultural (SIC), Gobierno de México

facts.text: In the Ayuuk language the word for a festival is xëëw, which also means day, sun, time and name.

source.title: Mixes : Pueblos indígenas México : Sistema de Información Cultural-Secretaría de Cultura
source.publisher: Secretaría de Cultura, Sistema de Información Cultural (SIC), Gobierno de México

nations.name: Maya
nations.lands: Yucatán, Campeche and Quintana Roo, on Mexico's Yucatán Peninsula

facts.text: La Voz de los Mayas, an INPI radio station broadcasting from Peto, Yucatán since 1982, reaches 677 localities across the peninsula in Maya and Spanish.

source.title: XEPET La Voz de los Mayas (AM) : Radio cultural indígena México : Sistema de Información Cultural-Secretaría de Cultura
source.publisher: Secretaría de Cultura, Sistema de Información Cultural (SIC), with station information from INPI

facts.text: In Felipe Carrillo Puerto, Quintana Roo, the INPI station La Voz del Gran Pueblo builds its programming with a citizen council of 25 people from 20 communities.

source.title: XHNKA La Voz del Gran Pueblo (FM) : Radio cultural indígena México : Sistema de Información Cultural-Secretaría de Cultura
source.publisher: Secretaría de Cultura, Sistema de Información Cultural (SIC), with station information from INPI

nations.name: Tsa ju jmí'
nations.lands: La Chinantla in northeastern Oaxaca, Mexico, and resettled communities in Veracruz

facts.text: Since November 18, 1991, La Voz de la Chinantla, an INPI station in San Lucas Ojitlán, has broadcast with bilingual Chinantec, Mazatec and Cuicatec staff.

source.title: XEOJN La Voz de la Chinantla (AM) : Radio cultural indígena México : Sistema de Información Cultural-Secretaría de Cultura
source.publisher: Secretaría de Cultura, Sistema de Información Cultural (SIC), with station information from INPI

facts.text: Chinantecs call themselves tsa ju jmí', people of the ancient word; each town also has its own name, beginning with tsa, dsa or alla, meaning people.

source.title: Chinantecos : Pueblos indígenas México : Sistema de Información Cultural-Secretaría de Cultura
source.publisher: Secretaría de Cultura, Sistema de Información Cultural (SIC), Gobierno de México

nations.name: Jñatrjo
nations.lands: The northwestern State of Mexico and eastern Michoacán, Mexico

facts.text: La Voz de la Sierra Oriente, on air since 1998 for Mazahua and Otomí communities, hosts poetry recitals and rock concerts in their own languages.

source.title: XETUX La Voz de la Sierra Oriente (AM) : Radio cultural indígena México : Sistema de Información Cultural-Secretaría de Cultura
source.publisher: Secretaría de Cultura, Sistema de Información Cultural (SIC), with station information from INPI

facts.text: In Mazahua and Otomí communities, their own normative systems guide shared work, forest care, land tenure and the election of community authorities.

source.title: XETUX La Voz de la Sierra Oriente (AM) : Radio cultural indígena México : Sistema de Información Cultural-Secretaría de Cultura
source.publisher: Secretaría de Cultura, Sistema de Información Cultural (SIC), with station information from INPI

nations.name: Ha shuta enima
nations.lands: The Sierra Mazateca of northern Oaxaca around Huautla de Jiménez, Mexico, and nearby parts of Veracruz

facts.text: The sound archive of La Voz de la Chinantla, an INPI station in Oaxaca, holds over 5,000 music recordings, including Mazatec huehuentones musicians.

source.title: XEOJN La Voz de la Chinantla (AM) : Radio cultural indígena México : Sistema de Información Cultural-Secretaría de Cultura
source.publisher: Secretaría de Cultura, Sistema de Información Cultural (SIC), with station information from INPI

facts.text: Mazatecs call themselves Ha shuta enima, which in their language means those who work the hills, humble people of custom.

source.title: Mazatecos : Pueblos indígenas México : Sistema de Información Cultural-Secretaría de Cultura
source.publisher: Secretaría de Cultura, Sistema de Información Cultural (SIC), Gobierno de México

nations.name: Triqui
nations.lands: Western Oaxaca, Mexico: a lower zone centered on San Juan Copala and an upper zone centered on San Andrés Chicahuaxtla

facts.text: La Voz de la Mixteca, an INPI radio station in Tlaxiaco, Oaxaca, broadcasts in Mixtec, Triqui and Spanish.

source.title: XETLA La Voz de la Mixteca (AM) : Radio cultural indígena México : Sistema de Información Cultural-Secretaría de Cultura
source.publisher: Secretaría de Cultura, Sistema de Información Cultural (SIC), with station information from INPI

facts.text: The name Triqui comes from driqui in the Triqui language, built from words meaning father and great or superior.

source.title: Triquis : Pueblos indígenas México : Sistema de Información Cultural-Secretaría de Cultura
source.publisher: Secretaría de Cultura, Sistema de Información Cultural (SIC), Gobierno de México

nations.name: Nahua
nations.lands: Many states of central and southern Mexico, including Puebla, Veracruz, Hidalgo, Guerrero, San Luis Potosí, the State of Mexico, Morelos, Tlaxcala and Mexico City

facts.text: XEZON, an INPI radio station in the Sierra de Zongolica, Veracruz, serves Nahua communities; relatives working in the United States can hear family on its programs by phone.

source.title: XEZON La Voz de la Sierra de Zongolica (AM) : Radio cultural indígena México : Sistema de Información Cultural-Secretaría de Cultura
source.publisher: Secretaría de Cultura, Sistema de Información Cultural (SIC), with station information from INPI

facts.text: In Mexico City alone, Nahua towns organize 700 festivities a year, most honoring the patron saints of towns and neighborhoods, and mayordomías are in charge of organizing them.

source.title: Pueblos Nahuas : Pueblos indígenas México : Sistema de Información Cultural-Secretaría de Cultura
source.publisher: Secretaría de Cultura, Sistema de Información Cultural (SIC), Gobierno de México

nations.name: Ñuu Savi
nations.lands: La Mixteca, in northwestern Oaxaca, southern Puebla and eastern Guerrero, Mexico, with migrant communities across Mexico and in the United States

facts.text: La Voz de la Mixteca, an INPI station in Tlaxiaco, Oaxaca, serves Mixtec, Triqui and Chocholtec peoples and has streamed online since 2006, reaching migrants in the United States.

source.title: XETLA La Voz de la Mixteca (AM) : Radio cultural indígena México : Sistema de Información Cultural-Secretaría de Cultura
source.publisher: Secretaría de Cultura, Sistema de Información Cultural (SIC), with station information from INPI

facts.text: Palm weaving holds a special place in the Mixteca economy: artisans make hats, mats, purses, toys and brooms, and children start learning crafts around age six.

source.title: Mixtecos (Guerrero, Oaxaca y Puebla) : Pueblos indígenas México : Sistema de Información Cultural-Secretaría de Cultura
source.publisher: Secretaría de Cultura, Sistema de Información Cultural (SIC), Gobierno de México

nations.name: Nn'anncue
nations.lands: The Sierra of the Costa Chica on the Guerrero and Oaxaca border, Mexico, including Xochistlahuaca, San Pedro Amuzgos and Santa María Ipalapa

facts.text: After a struggle that began in 1920, Amuzgo lands were restored as an ejido on August 25, 1933, covering 6,384 hectares.

source.title: Amuzgos : Pueblos indígenas México : Sistema de Información Cultural-Secretaría de Cultura
source.publisher: Secretaría de Cultura, Sistema de Información Cultural (SIC), Gobierno de México

facts.text: Amuzgo women weave huipiles, rebozos and tablecloths on the backstrap loom, while men make bamboo and palm baskets.

source.title: Amuzgos : Pueblos indígenas México : Sistema de Información Cultural-Secretaría de Cultura
source.publisher: Secretaría de Cultura, Sistema de Información Cultural (SIC), Gobierno de México

nations.name: Kitsé Cha'tnio
nations.lands: Southwestern Oaxaca, Mexico, near the Pacific coast, including Juquila, Yaitepec, Quiahije and Nopala

facts.text: Since 1994, La Voz de la Costa Chica in Santiago Jamiltepec, Oaxaca has broadcast in Mixtec, Amuzgo, Chatino, Tacuate and Spanish.

source.title: XEJAM La Voz de la Costa Chica (AM) : Radio cultural indígena México : Sistema de Información Cultural-Secretaría de Cultura
source.publisher: Secretaría de Cultura, Sistema de Información Cultural (SIC), with station information from INPI

facts.text: Chatino weaving and embroidery continue in Yaitepec, Quiahije and Nopala, where blouses, shoulder bags, sashes and tablecloths are made.

source.title: Chatinos : Pueblos indígenas México : Sistema de Información Cultural-Secretaría de Cultura
source.publisher: Secretaría de Cultura, Sistema de Información Cultural (SIC), Gobierno de México

nations.name: O' de püt
nations.lands: Northwestern and central Chiapas, Mexico, including Copainalá, Ocotepec, Tapalapa, Tecpatán, Ocozocoautla and Tuxtla Gutiérrez

facts.text: Since 1997, the INPI station La Voz de los Vientos has broadcast from Copainalá, a town whose Zoque name is Pokiomä, in Zoque, Tsotsil and Spanish.

source.title: XECOPA La Voz de los Vientos (AM) : Radio cultural indígena México : Sistema de Información Cultural-Secretaría de Cultura
source.publisher: Secretaría de Cultura, Sistema de Información Cultural (SIC), with station information from INPI

facts.text: In Ocotepec, Zoque artisans make wacas, vine baskets for washing coffee and cacao beans, sold through the Casa de las Artesanías de Chiapas.

source.title: Zoques : Pueblos indígenas México : Sistema de Información Cultural-Secretaría de Cultura
source.publisher: Secretaría de Cultura, Sistema de Información Cultural (SIC), Gobierno de México

nations.name: Gwich'in
nations.lands: Northeast Alaska, including Fort Yukon, Venetie and Arctic Village, plus northern Yukon and the Northwest Territories in Canada

facts.text: Dinjii Zhuh K'yaa, the Gwich'in language, is one of ten Doyon region languages for which Doyon Languages Online is creating introductory online lessons.
Gwich'in Council International represents about 9,000 Gwich'in in Alaska, Yukon and the Northwest Territories as a Permanent Participant in the Arctic Council.

nations.name: St. Lawrence Island Yupik
nations.lands: Gambell and Savoonga on St. Lawrence Island in the Bering Sea, Alaska, United States; close relatives live on the Chukchi Peninsula across the Bering Strait

facts.text: St. Lawrence Island Yupik is almost the same language as the one spoken just across the Bering Strait, at the tip of Siberia's Chukchi Peninsula.

source.title: Languages - Siberian Yupik
source.publisher: Alaska Native Language Center, University of Alaska Fairbanks

facts.text: The Alaska Native Language Center reports that children in Gambell and Savoonga learn St. Lawrence Island Yupik as the first language of the home.

source.title: Languages - Siberian Yupik
source.publisher: Alaska Native Language Center, University of Alaska Fairbanks

nations.name: Unangax̂
nations.lands: Aleutian Islands, Pribilof Islands and the western Alaska Peninsula, Alaska, United States

facts.text: Students in APIA's 2025 Unangam Tunuu Summer Language Intensive learned from Unangax̂ Elders, and APIA holds a weekly Unangam Tunuu Community Night in Anchorage.
Unangam Tunuu is a single language with eastern and western dialects that divide at Atka Island.

source.title: Languages - Unangam Tunuu / Aleut
source.publisher: Alaska Native Language Center, University of Alaska Fairbanks

nations.name: Haida
nations.lands: Southern Prince of Wales Island, including Hydaburg, Kasaan and Craig, and Ketchikan, Southeast Alaska, United States

facts.text: Kasaan's 'Láa Náay Justice System works to keep the peace and promote wellness by addressing problems through culturally appropriate methods.
The Organized Village of Kasaan, a Haida tribal government, works to promote, preserve and protect Haida identity and values for its elders and youth.

nations.name: Tsimshian
nations.lands: Metlakatla on the Annette Islands Reserve, Southeast Alaska, United States; Tsimshian homelands continue in British Columbia, Canada

facts.text: The Hyaak Foundation in Metlakatla works to keep Sm'algyax, the Tsimshian language, alive and well.
The Metlakatla Indian Community on the Annette Islands holds the only Indian reserve in Alaska.

nations.name: Lower Tanana Dene
nations.lands: Nenana, Minto and the Fairbanks area along the Tanana River, Interior Alaska, United States

facts.text: Benhti Kenaga', the Lower Tanana language, is one of ten Doyon region languages for which Doyon Languages Online is creating introductory online lessons.
A pocket dictionary of the Lower Tanana language, which is spoken in Nenana and Minto on the Tanana River, was published in 2009.

source.title: Languages - Tanana
source.publisher: Alaska Native Language Center, University of Alaska Fairbanks

nations.name: Deg Hit'an
nations.lands: Shageluk, Anvik and Holy Cross on the lower Yukon River, Alaska, United States

facts.text: Deg Xinag is one of ten Doyon region languages for which Doyon Languages Online is creating introductory online lessons.
Learners can use a free online Deg Xinag dictionary with sound recordings, available through the Alaska Native Knowledge Network.

source.title: Languages - Deg Xinag
source.publisher: Alaska Native Language Center, University of Alaska Fairbanks

nations.name: Native Village of Eklutna
nations.lands: Alaska; the Tribal government describes community work in Eklutna Village and Anchorage

facts.text: The Tribe describes its government as traditional rather than formed under the Indian Reorganization Act, with seven Council members serving staggered three-year terms.
The Tribe reports working with partners on assessment, planning and restoration of the Eklutna River. The page describes ongoing work, not a completed restoration.

nations.name: Native Hawaiians
nations.lands: The Hawaiian Islands (Hawaiʻi), United States

facts.text: The Office of Hawaiian Affairs, approved by Hawaiʻi voters in 1978 to serve Native Hawaiians, is governed by nine trustees elected statewide for four-year terms.
Since a 1978 amendment to the state constitution, Hawaiian and English have both been official languages of the State of Hawaiʻi.

source.title: State Constitution
source.publisher: Legislative Reference Bureau, State of Hawaiʻi

nations.name: Eyak
nations.lands: Cordova, the Copper River Delta and Prince William Sound, Alaska, United States

facts.text: The Native Village of Eyak in Cordova is a federally recognized tribe that unites Eyak, Chugach Region, Tlingit and Athabaskan peoples.

source.title: Native Village of Eyak - About Us

facts.text: Eyak is not an Athabascan language but its own branch beside the Athabascan languages, within the Athabascan-Eyak-Tlingit language family.

source.title: Languages - Eyak
source.publisher: Alaska Native Language Center, University of Alaska Fairbanks

nations.name: Yup'ik
nations.lands: Yukon-Kuskokwim Delta and nearby coasts and rivers of southwest Alaska, United States

facts.text: In the Calista Region along the Yukon and Kuskokwim rivers, subsistence hunting, fishing and gathering bind communities together and are part of who people are.
The word Yup'ik names both the language and the people, built from yuk, meaning person, and pik, meaning real.

source.title: Languages - Central Yup'ik
source.publisher: Alaska Native Language Center, University of Alaska Fairbanks

nations.name: Kággaba
nations.lands: Northern, eastern and western slopes of the Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta in La Guajira, Magdalena and Cesar, Colombia

facts.text: The Organización Gonawindúa Tayrona serves as the representative body of the Kággaba people's own Indigenous government.
The Kággaba speak their own language, often called Kogui, which belongs to the Chibcha language family.

source.title: Kaggabba (Kogui): los guardianes de la armonía del mundo
source.publisher: Ministerio de Cultura de Colombia, Dirección de Poblaciones

nations.name: Quechua
nations.lands: Andean highlands and valleys of Peru and Bolivia, with Quechua communities also in Argentina and Chile

facts.text: Peru's Ministry of Culture lists Quechua as a vital language, and the 2017 census counted 3,805,531 people who learned to speak it in childhood.

source.title: Quechuas | BDPI
source.publisher: Ministerio de Cultura del Perú, Base de Datos de Pueblos Indígenas u Originarios

facts.text: Peru's Ministry of Culture reports that 5,179,774 people nationwide feel or consider themselves part of the Quechua peoples.

source.title: Quechuas | BDPI
source.publisher: Ministerio de Cultura del Perú, Base de Datos de Pueblos Indígenas u Originarios

nations.name: Diaguita
nations.lands: Huasco and Choapa valleys of Chile's Norte Chico, and northwestern Argentina

facts.text: The first Diaguita community constituted under Chile's Indigenous Law, the Estancia Agrícola Diaguita de los Huascoaltinos, formed in 2006.
Many people who self-identify as Diaguita in Chile live in the upper Huasco River basin, in the municipality of Alto del Carmen.

nations.name: Kichwa Otavalo
nations.lands: Otavalo and nearby communities such as Peguche in Imbabura province, northern Ecuador

facts.text: Hampiriypacha, a Kichwa Otavalo association of seed guardians, works to protect knowledge that women have passed down for generations.

source.title: Meet our 2022 Keepers of the Earth Fund Grant Partners

facts.text: Yarina, a Kichwa Otavalo family band started in 1984, plays original Indigenous rhythms on traditional Andean instruments and works to keep Kichwa traditions alive.

nations.name: Kichwa Puruwá
nations.lands: Chimborazo province in the central highlands of Ecuador

facts.text: The Puruwá people include the communities of Cacha, Colta, Licto and Guamote in Chimborazo, each with its own local character.

source.title: Guía Nacional de Nutrición de las Nacionalidades y Pueblos Indígenas, Afroecuatoriano y Montubio
source.publisher: Ministerio de Salud Pública del Ecuador

facts.text: Ecuador's 2010 census counted 136,141 Kichwa Puruwá people, about 18.5 percent of the whole Kichwa nationality.

source.title: Guía Nacional de Nutrición de las Nacionalidades y Pueblos Indígenas, Afroecuatoriano y Montubio
source.publisher: Ministerio de Salud Pública del Ecuador

nations.name: Nasa
nations.lands: Cauca department, especially Tierradentro and northern Cauca, with communities in Huila, Valle del Cauca, Tolima and Putumayo, Colombia

facts.text: In 1971 Indigenous communities of Cauca founded the CRIC to recover resguardo lands, strengthen their cabildos and defend their history, language and customs.

source.title: Nasa (Paez), la gente del agua
source.publisher: Ministerio de Cultura de Colombia, Dirección de Poblaciones

facts.text: The Nasa language is Nasa Yuwe. In Colombia's 2005 census, 41.9 percent of Nasa people reported speaking it.

source.title: Nasa (Paez), la gente del agua
source.publisher: Ministerio de Cultura de Colombia, Dirección de Poblaciones

nations.name: Aymara
nations.lands: The altiplano around Lake Titicaca and nearby valleys and cities of Bolivia and Peru, and the far north of Chile

facts.text: Aymara is a vital language in Peru, where the 2017 census counted 450,010 people who learned to speak it in childhood.

source.title: Aimara | BDPI
source.publisher: Ministerio de Cultura del Perú, Base de Datos de Pueblos Indígenas u Originarios

facts.text: In Bolivia's 2024 census, more than one million people self-identified as Aymara, and more than one million as Quechua.

source.title: INE presenta resultados del Censo 2024 que muestran la transformación demográfica y avances sociales en Bolivia
source.publisher: Instituto Nacional de Estadística de Bolivia

nations.name: Wiwa
nations.lands: Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta in La Guajira, Cesar and Magdalena, Colombia

facts.text: Most young Wiwa speak three languages: Damana, their mother tongue, the neighboring Kogui language, and Spanish.

source.title: Wiwa: la gente que da origen al calor
source.publisher: Ministerio de Cultura de Colombia, Dirección de Poblaciones

facts.text: Through education policies the Wiwa established an alphabet for Damana, and they are working to have it taught alongside Spanish in schools.

source.title: Wiwa: la gente que da origen al calor
source.publisher: Ministerio de Cultura de Colombia, Dirección de Poblaciones

nations.name: Kichwa Kañari
nations.lands: Cañar and Azuay provinces in the southern highlands of Ecuador

facts.text: In Cañar parish, the province's largest Indigenous organizational network brings together 15 communities and 5 cooperatives.

source.title: Guía Nacional de Nutrición de las Nacionalidades y Pueblos Indígenas, Afroecuatoriano y Montubio
source.publisher: Ministerio de Salud Pública del Ecuador

facts.text: The Kañari keep a vigorous ethnic identity and a very strong organizational system, in which cooperatives and many kinds of organizations are very active.

source.title: Guía Nacional de Nutrición de las Nacionalidades y Pueblos Indígenas, Afroecuatoriano y Montubio
source.publisher: Ministerio de Salud Pública del Ecuador

nations.name: Misak
nations.lands: Resguardos of Guambía and Quisgó in Silvia, Cauca, and nearby municipalities of southwestern Colombia

facts.text: The Misak keep their mother tongue, Wampi-misamerawam, and see it as central to their ethnic and cultural identity.

source.title: Misak (Guambianos), la gente del agua, del conocimiento y de los sueños
source.publisher: Ministerio de Cultura de Colombia, Dirección de Poblaciones

facts.text: In 2000 a Misak leader became the first Indigenous person elected by popular vote as governor of Colombia's Cauca department.

source.title: Misak (Guambianos), la gente del agua, del conocimiento y de los sueños
source.publisher: Ministerio de Cultura de Colombia, Dirección de Poblaciones

nations.name: Kichwa Kayambi
nations.lands: Around Cayambe in Pichincha province and neighboring areas of Imbabura, northern Ecuador

facts.text: In 2022 Kayambi water boards, communes and community organizations met with a national legislator to discuss issues including a new water law.

source.title: Asamblea ampliada y mesa de trabajo con el Pueblo Kayambi

facts.text: The Confederación del Pueblo Kayambi holds a General Assembly where its communities and organizations bring their proposals and demands.

source.title: Asamblea General con el Pueblo Kayambi

nations.name: Mansi
nations.lands: Ob and Irtysh basin in western Siberia, mainly Khanty-Mansi Autonomous Okrug (Yugra), with small groups in Yamal-Nenets Autonomous Okrug and Sverdlovsk Oblast, Russia

facts.text: Luima Seripos, a newspaper in the Mansi language, first came out on 11 February 1989 and is still produced today in a joint newsroom with the Khanty paper.

source.title: Историческая справка
source.publisher: Khanty Mansi Mir (joint editorial office of the Khanty Yasang and Luima Seripos newspapers)

facts.text: Mansi rapper Yevgeny Anyamov, known as Bizzo, records his songs in Mansi and opened his own studio in his hometown of Ivdel to share his people's culture with youth.

nations.name: Nivkh
nations.lands: Lower Amur River in Khabarovsk Krai and Sakhalin Island, Russia

facts.text: The Nivkh speak a language isolate, probably one of the oldest languages of Eurasia. Its links to other languages have not been established.

source.title: Нивхи
source.publisher: RAIPON (Association of Indigenous Small-Numbered Peoples of the North, Siberia and the Far East)

facts.text: Nivkh life was built on fishing and hunting, including sea mammals taken with spears or with nets woven from leather straps.

source.title: Нивхи
source.publisher: RAIPON (Association of Indigenous Small-Numbered Peoples of the North, Siberia and the Far East)

nations.name: Luoravetlan
nations.lands: Chukotka Autonomous Okrug, northern Kamchatka Krai and the Nizhnekolymsky District of Sakha (Yakutia), Russia

facts.text: Researchers at Russia's Kunstkamera museum published a 2018 study on the mobile dwellings of Chukchi reindeer herders, covering both traditions and innovations.

source.title: Arctic Research Center
source.publisher: Peter the Great Museum of Anthropology and Ethnography (Kunstkamera), Russian Academy of Sciences

facts.text: Carving bone and walrus ivory and embroidering with reindeer hair are long-standing Chukchi arts, practised alongside reindeer herding and hunting.

source.title: Чукчи
source.publisher: RAIPON (Association of Indigenous Small-Numbered Peoples of the North, Siberia and the Far East)

nations.name: Even
nations.lands: Northeastern Siberia: Sakha (Yakutia), Magadan Oblast, Kamchatka, Chukotka and Khabarovsk Krai, Russia

facts.text: The Even language belongs to the Tungusic (Manchu-Tungus) branch and is close to Evenki. Even self-names include Even (local) and Orochel (reindeer people).

source.title: Эвены
source.publisher: RAIPON (Association of Indigenous Small-Numbered Peoples of the North, Siberia and the Far East)

facts.text: The 2002 census counted 11,657 Even living in the Republic of Sakha (Yakutia).

source.title: Эвены
source.publisher: RAIPON (Association of Indigenous Small-Numbered Peoples of the North, Siberia and the Far East)

nations.name: Itelmen
nations.lands: Tigilsky District on the west coast of Kamchatka Krai, with smaller groups in Chukotka and Magadan Oblast, Russia

facts.text: Western Itelmen is the Itelmen language that has been kept to the present day.

source.title: Ительмены
source.publisher: RAIPON (Association of Indigenous Small-Numbered Peoples of the North, Siberia and the Far East)

facts.text: Fishing, above all for salmon, is the traditional Itelmen livelihood on Kamchatka.

source.title: Ительмены
source.publisher: RAIPON (Association of Indigenous Small-Numbered Peoples of the North, Siberia and the Far East)

nations.name: Ket
nations.lands: Yenisei River basin, mainly Turukhansky District of Krasnoyarsk Krai, Russia

facts.text: A Cyrillic writing system that Ket speakers actually use came into being in the late 1980s.

source.title: Кеты
source.publisher: RAIPON (Association of Indigenous Small-Numbered Peoples of the North, Siberia and the Far East)

facts.text: Ket is the only living language of the Yeniseian language family.

source.title: Кеты
source.publisher: RAIPON (Association of Indigenous Small-Numbered Peoples of the North, Siberia and the Far East)

nations.name: Inughuit
nations.lands: Avanersuaq (the Thule region) in northwest Greenland, centred on the town of Qaanaaq

facts.text: Hunting is still a significant part of the livelihood of several families in Qaanaaq, Greenland's youngest and northernmost town.
The Inughuit have their own language, or dialect, and a hunting culture that is distinctive in several ways.

nations.name: Yupik
nations.lands: Settlements on the eastern coast of the Chukchi Peninsula, Chukotka Autonomous Okrug, Russia, across the Bering Strait from Alaska

facts.text: Inuit from Chukotka became part of the Inuit Circumpolar Council in 1992, a goal that was in ICC's vision from the very beginning.
Yupik hunters are regarded as originators of traditional whaling in the region, hunting walrus, seal and whale with harpoons.

source.title: Эскимосы
source.publisher: RAIPON (Association of Indigenous Small-Numbered Peoples of the North, Siberia and the Far East)

nations.name: Evenki
nations.lands: Siberian taiga from the Ob River to the Sea of Okhotsk, with the largest group in Sakha (Yakutia), also Krasnoyarsk and Khabarovsk krais, Buryatia, Amur, Irkutsk and Zabaykalsky regions of Russia, and in China and Mongolia

facts.text: Evenki communities live across Russia, with the largest in Sakha (Yakutia), and Evenki also live in China and Mongolia.

source.title: Эвенки
source.publisher: RAIPON (Association of Indigenous Small-Numbered Peoples of the North, Siberia and the Far East)

facts.text: Evenki homelands span a huge part of the Siberian taiga, from the Ob River in the west to the Sea of Okhotsk in the east.

source.title: The Evenks
source.publisher: The Red Book of the Peoples of the Russian Empire (Institute of the Estonian Language archive)

nations.name: Dolgan
nations.lands: Taimyr Peninsula in Krasnoyarsk Krai (Taimyr Dolgan-Nenets District) and the Anabar District and city of Yakutsk in Sakha (Yakutia), Russia

facts.text: During an August 2026 folk culture expedition to Khatanga, the Dolgan dried-fish dish kerdiileek was added to the list of Taimyr's intangible cultural heritage.

source.title: Долганская юкола «кэрдиилээк» признана объектом нематериального наследия Таймыра
source.publisher: RAIPON (Association of Indigenous Small-Numbered Peoples of the North, Siberia and the Far East)

facts.text: Dolgan is a Turkic language, close to Sakha (Yakut), from which it separated through isolated development.

source.title: Долганы
source.publisher: RAIPON (Association of Indigenous Small-Numbered Peoples of the North, Siberia and the Far East)

nations.name: Wajãpi
nations.lands: Wajãpi Indigenous Land in Amapá, Brazil, and the middle and upper Oyapock River in French Guiana

facts.text: In 1994 the Wajãpi began demarcating their own Indigenous Land in Amapá, Brazil, and founded the Council of Wajãpi Villages, known as Apina.

source.title: Wajãpi
source.publisher: Instituto Socioambiental (ISA), Indigenous Peoples in Brazil

facts.text: In French Guiana the Wayãpi live along the middle and upper Oyapock River.

nations.name: Wayana
nations.lands: Upper Maroni River and its tributaries in French Guiana, the Tapanahony and Paloemeu rivers in Suriname, and the East Paru River in Pará, Brazil

facts.text: France recognizes Wayana as one of six Amerindian languages of French Guiana with the status of a language of France.

source.title: Langues de France et langues régionales en Guyane: bilan au 7 décembre 2015
source.publisher: Ministère de la Culture, Direction des affaires culturelles de Guyane

facts.text: Among younger people on Brazil's East Paru River, the Wayana language has gained great prestige.

source.title: Wayana
source.publisher: Instituto Socioambiental (ISA), Indigenous Peoples in Brazil

nations.name: Uwottüja
nations.lands: The Autana, Cuao, Sipapo and Guayapo rivers and the middle Orinoco, Amazonas state, Venezuela

facts.text: In 2020 Uwottüja communities of the Autana, Cuao, Sipapo and Guayapo rivers met at Pendare and declared themselves guardians of their territory.

source.title: Pronunciamiento del Pueblo Indígena Uwottüja de los habitantes de los cuatro ríos Autana, Cuao, Sipapo, Guayapo y el sector Orinoco Medio
source.publisher: Pueblo Indígena Uwottüja, published by the Observatorio de Ecología Política de Venezuela

facts.text: The Uwottüja held their first congress as a people in 1984, uniting around the defense of their ancestral lands 'like one churuata, with one voice'.

source.title: Pronunciamiento del Pueblo Indígena Uwottüja de los habitantes de los cuatro ríos Autana, Cuao, Sipapo, Guayapo y el sector Orinoco Medio
source.publisher: Pueblo Indígena Uwottüja, published by the Observatorio de Ecología Política de Venezuela

nations.name: Ye'kwana
nations.lands: Amazonas and Bolívar states in southern Venezuela, and the Auaris and Uraricoera rivers of Roraima, Brazil

facts.text: The name Ye'kwana, which the people use for themselves, entered Venezuela's census in 1982 and has almost fully replaced the outside name Makiritare.

source.title: Censo Nacional de Población y Vivienda 2011: Empadronamiento de la Población Indígena

facts.text: Among themselves the Ye'kwana use So'to, meaning 'people', while Ye'kwana can be translated as 'canoe people'.

source.title: Ye'kwana
source.publisher: Instituto Socioambiental (ISA), Indigenous Peoples in Brazil

nations.name: Teko
nations.lands: Camopi on the Oyapock River and Cayodé on the upper Maroni, French Guiana

facts.text: France lists Teko, formerly called Émerillon, among French Guiana's six Amerindian languages recognized as languages of France.

source.title: Langues de France et langues régionales en Guyane: bilan au 7 décembre 2015
source.publisher: Ministère de la Culture, Direction des affaires culturelles de Guyane

facts.text: Teko and Wayãpi are the two Tupi-Guarani languages spoken in the Amazonian Park of French Guiana, where Wayana belongs to the Carib family.

nations.name: Pemón
nations.lands: Savannas of southeastern Venezuela, the Kamarang River area of Guyana, and Roraima state in Brazil

facts.text: Taurepang, Arekuna and Kamarakoto communities share the self-name Pemon, a word meaning 'people' or 'us'.

source.title: Taurepang
source.publisher: Instituto Socioambiental (ISA), Indigenous Peoples in Brazil

facts.text: In Guyana, Arekuna communities live on the banks of the Kamarang River.

source.title: Indigenous Nations
source.publisher: Ministry of Amerindian Affairs, Government of Guyana

nations.name: Akawaio
nations.lands: Upper Mazaruni area and nearby river valleys of western Guyana, with Akawaio also counted in Venezuela's census

facts.text: Akawaio is one of the nine Indigenous languages covered by Guyana's language revival programme, which the government moved to restart in 2021.

source.title: Gov't to resume Amerindian language revival project
source.publisher: Department of Public Information, Government of Guyana

facts.text: Kapohn is the Akawaio people's own name for themselves, and like most peoples of Guyana's interior they are Carib speakers.

nations.name: Barí
nations.lands: Serranía de los Motilones and the Catatumbo and Oro river basins in Norte de Santander, Colombia, and Zulia state, Venezuela

facts.text: The Barí language, of the Chibcha family, is being passed on to new generations and has speakers of all ages.
Barí live in the foothills of Colombia's Serranía de los Motilones along the Catatumbo and Oro rivers, with settlements also in Zulia state, Venezuela.
